How sticky is inflation? Let's see: Before i go on... some news to be aware of: There are rumors of a Russian media saying there is an Iran-US deal Back to the data agenda... eyes on the Australian July month CPI data today.

Monthly CPI data used to be very much in second place compared to the quarterly data, but not any more.

I'll get a preview of today's data posted separately (ADDED, here it is: Preview - Australia's July CPI set to ease to 3.2-3.3pct as trimmed mean holds near 3.5pct ).

Until then, as background info: Australia's shift to a monthly Consumer Price Index as the nation's primary inflation measure marks the most significant change to the country's price statistics in decades, ending the quarterly release's century-long role as the headline benchmark for monetary policy.

The transition traces back to September 2022, when the Australian Bureau of Statistics introduced a monthly CPI indicator to give policymakers and markets an earlier read on inflation between quarterly releases.

That early indicator drew on existing data collection methods and updated prices for roughly two thirds of the CPI basket each month, using data the ABS was already gathering for the quarterly series.

At the time, the ABS and the Reserve Bank both flagged that the quarterly CPI would likely remain the principal measure for the foreseeable future, given large parts of the basket, particularly consumer durables and many administered prices, were only priced once a quarter.

That changed as the ABS invested in broader monthly price collection.

Scoreboard update: An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.

Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.
